$comment: Prose allowlists rot — issue #12 records a case where a recorded list was written from
memory and omitted three of four real hits — so this is data the script reads, and the
script's own test suite asserts every entry is still needed.
Omitting both predicates allowlists the whole file for that invariant. Supplying both
narrows the entry: a line must satisfy both. No shape can widen an exemption from a
code-level window, because nothing in a byte radius can be staleness-checked.
Every entry below is a MENTION-TO-FORBID: the text names a forbidden shape in order to
forbid it. Dropping the mention would delete the rule it carries. The one exception is
`skill-references`, which allowlists a token that is not a command at all.

specs-roots.contains: never search for a spec under a bare

plan-package-prefix.contains: This rule owns the `{{PLAN_PACKAGE}}` placeholder convention

skill-references.$note: `/ws` is a FastAPI WebSocket route, not a command. Needed as of b359a6c by the three live mentions below; when the last of them goes, the staleness test in test_check_invariants.py fails and this entry must go with it.
Second and last file that mentions the route: axb-implement's Definition-of-Done example.

section-references.$note: A `§` on a line naming a licence refers to that licence, not to STANDARDS.md. Line-scoped on purpose: the 16-char lookbehind this replaced required the literal `Apache-N.N ` spelling, so `Apache License 2.0 §11(x)` and `Apache-2.0, §11(x)` failed the gate falsely. The staleness test proves the pattern still matches a line here; it does not prove the exemption is load-bearing, because today's only citation (`§4(d)`) resolves against STANDARDS.md anyway.
